For boundary handling at the global domain edges, I need clamping so ranks at z=0 or z=nz-1 treat their own boundary plane as its own neighbor -- this gets tricky if the number of z-planes is smaller than the number of processes, since some ranks would end up with zero planes and complicate the halo exchange logic, so I'm thinking through how to distribute planes robustly using floor/ceil counts while handling the zero-plane edge case cleanly.\n\nWith base=0, active ranks form a contiguous prefix 0..nz-1, so neighbor logic simplifies: up neighbor is r+1 if within active count, else MPI_PROC_NULL, making Sendrecv a no-op for inactive ranks since their loops are empty anyway. I'll verify by building both versions with matching flags and comparing their output hashes directly, and I also need to check the global min/max/range reduction logic across MPI ranks.\n\nFor exact output reproduction, since rank order matches z-order in the slab decomposition, I can gather the full field to rank 0 with MPI_Gatherv and print only there, giving exact layout equivalence with the original. Min/max via Allreduce is already exact regardless of summation order, so that part is safe — the main concern now is avoiding costly full gathers every step and instead overlapping communication with computation during normal runs.\n\nMy plan is to split each timestep into interior and boundary work: post nonblocking halo exchanges for concentration, compute mu on interior z-planes while halos are in flight, then finish boundary mu once halos arrive, exchange mu halos, and repeat the same interior/boundary split for the concentration update. I need to special-case thin slabs (nzl < 3) where there's no true interior, and I'm considering padding each field array with extra halo planes so plane access stays uniform across interior and boundary cases.\n\nI'm realizing I can avoid clamping logic along z entirely by keeping ghost planes updated — at global domain edges the ghost just mirrors the boundary plane itself, so the same neighbor-access kernel works everywhere without special-casing true boundaries versus halo boundaries.\n\nMu needs the same ghost-exchange treatment since cnew depends on neighboring mu values, and with per-rank slabs the halo exchange is just a plane of nx*ny doubles sent up and down via nonblocking MPI calls — simple point-to-point is fine here rather than persistent requests. I'll wrap the overall logic in a helper function so MPI_Finalize is called cleanly before returning from main.\n\nI also want to preserve the original's slightly undefined behavior with edge cases like zero grid sizes or negative iteration counts, just making sure these don't cause MPI-specific crashes—though I might slightly adjust validation to avoid touching empty arrays safely.\n\nFor the halo exchange between neighboring ranks, I'm working out which ghost plane indices get sent and received in each direction, handling boundary ranks by copying their own edge planes instead of communicating, and planning to use distinct message tags to avoid confusion between the up and down exchanges.\n\nNow I'm structuring the step loop to overlap communication with computation: posting the non-blocking sends and receives first, computing the interior mu values that don't depend on ghost data, then waiting on the halo exchange and filling in the boundary-adjacent planes afterward, while handling the edge case where a rank only owns a single plane.\n\nI'm double-checking that cold ghosts are valid wherever needed and that mu ghosts arrive before boundary cnew planes are computed, then considering whether cache-friendly loop ordering in the kernel's bounds-checked indexing would help, while keeping the implementation strictly MPI-only.\n\nI also need to watch floating-point contraction settings, since a build using gnu++20 defaults could enable fused multiply-add, subtly altering the arithmetic in the Laplacian stencil compared to a strict separate add/subtract/multiply sequence.\n\nGiven that, the safest path is to disable fp-contract explicitly in the build flags so results stay bit-reproducible, though that means building the baseline the same way for a fair comparison. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1792960889132,"sessionID":"ses_e8b363015ffezbf1BTPlN1i7yK","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01YAsW3vVcrKyNgACUg6thjJ","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cahn-hilliard_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r1/cahn-hilliard/cahn_hilliard.cpp","content":"#include <mpi.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Distributed-memory Cahn-Hilliard solver.\n//\n// The domain is split into contiguous slabs of z-planes, one slab per MPI rank\n// (ranks beyond nz own nothing). Each field is stored with one ghost plane below\n// (local index 0) and one above (local index nzl+1); owned planes are 1..nzl.\n// Ghost planes that lie across a rank boundary are filled by nonblocking halo\n// exchange. Ghost planes that lie outside the global domain hold a copy of the\n// nearest owned plane, which reproduces the clamped (Neumann-like) boundary of\n// the serial code exactly.\n//\n// Each time step is organised to hide communication:\n//   1. start halo exchange of c\n//   2. compute mu on interior planes (needs only owned c)\n//   3. finish halo exchange of c; compute mu on the two boundary planes\n//   4. start halo exchange of mu\n//   5. compute c_new on interior planes (needs only owned mu)\n//   6. finish halo exchange of mu; compute c_new on the two boundary planes\n// All stencil arithmetic is performed in the same order as the serial code, so\n// results are bitwise identical for any number of ranks.\n\nnamespace {\n\nstruct Params {\n    double dx, dy, dz;\n    double dt;\n    double e_AA, e_BB, e_AB;\n    double gamma;\n    double D;\n};\n\n// Owned z-planes of rank r: first plane index and count.\nvoid planeRange(size_t nz, size_t P, size_t r, size_t& z0, size_t& nzl) {\n    const size_t base = nz / P;\n    const size_t rem = nz % P;\n    nzl = base + (r < rem ? 1 : 0);\n    z0 = r * base + std::min(r, rem);\n}\n\nstruct Decomp {\n    MPI_Comm comm;\n    size_t nx, ny, nz;\n    size_t plane;   // nx * ny\n    size_t z0;      // first global z-plane owned by this rank\n    size_t nzl;     // number of owned z-planes\n    int down;       // rank owning the planes below, or MPI_PROC_NULL\n    int up;         // rank owning the planes above, or MPI_PROC_NULL\n};\n\nDecomp makeDecomp(MPI_Comm comm, int rank, int size, size_t nx, size_t ny, size_t nz) {\n    const size_t P = static_cast<size_t>(size);\n    const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(rank);\n    const size_t active = std::min(P, nz);  // ranks [0, active) own at least one plane\n\n    Decomp d{};\n    d.comm = comm;\n    d.nx = nx;\n    d.ny = ny;\n    d.nz = nz;\n    d.plane = nx * ny;\n    planeRange(nz, P, r, d.z0, d.nzl);\n    d.down = (r > 0 && r < active) ? rank - 1 : MPI_PROC_NULL;\n    d.up = (r + 1 < active) ? rank + 1 : MPI_PROC_NULL;\n    return d;\n}\n\n// Message tags: TAG_UP carries data moving to a higher rank, TAG_DOWN to a lower one.\nconstexpr int TAG_UP = 0;\nconstexpr int TAG_DOWN = 1;\n\n// Post nonblocking exchange of the boundary planes of field f (4 requests).\nvoid haloStart(const Decomp& d, double* f, MPI_Request* req) {\n    const int n = static_cast<int>(d.plane);\n    double* lowGhost = f;\n    double* lowOwned = f + d.plane;\n    double* highOwned = f + d.nzl * d.plane;\n    double* highGhost = f + (d.nzl + 1) * d.plane;\n\n    MPI_Irecv(lowGhost, n, MPI_DOUBLE, d.down, TAG_UP, d.comm, &req[0]);\n    MPI_Irecv(highGhost, n, MPI_DOUBLE, d.up, TAG_DOWN, d.comm, &req[1]);\n    MPI_Isend(highOwned, n, MPI_DOUBLE, d.up, TAG_UP, d.comm, &req[2]);\n    MPI_Isend(lowOwned, n, MPI_DOUBLE, d.down, TAG_DOWN, d.comm, &req[3]);\n}\n\n// Complete the exchange and refresh ghost planes on the global domain boundary.\nvoid haloFinish(const Decomp& d, double* f, MPI_Request* req) {\n    MPI_Waitall(4, req, MPI_STATUSES_IGNORE);\n    if (d.nzl == 0) return;\n\n    const size_t pl = d.plane;\n    if (d.down == MPI_PROC_NULL) {\n        std::copy(f + pl, f + 2 * pl, f);\n    }\n    if (d.up == MPI_PROC_NULL) {\n        std::copy(f + d.nzl * pl, f + (d.nzl + 1) * pl, f + (d.nzl + 1) * pl);\n    }\n}\n\n// Visit every x index of a row together with its clamped neighbours xp and xn.\ntemplate <typename F>\ninline void forEachX(size_t nx, F&& body) {\n    if (nx == 0) return;\n    if (nx == 1) {\n        body(size_t{0}, size_t{0}, size_t{0});\n        return;\n    }\n    body(size_t{0}, size_t{1}, size_t{0});\n    for (size_t x = 1; x + 1 < nx; ++x) {\n        body(x, x + 1, x - 1);\n    }\n    body(nx - 1, nx - 1, nx - 2);\n}\n\n// Pointers to the centre row and its six neighbour rows (clamped in y).\nstruct Row {\n    const double* c;\n    const double* up;\n    const double* dn;\n    const double* zp;\n    const double* zm;\n};\n\ninline Row rowAt(const double* f, const Decomp& d, size_t p, size_t y) {\n    const double* row = f + p * d.plane + y * d.nx;\n    return Row{\n        row,\n        (y + 1 < d.ny) ? row + d.nx : row,\n        (y > 0) ? row - d.nx : row,\n        row + d.plane,\n        row - d.plane,\n    };\n}\n\n// 7-point Laplacian with clamped boundaries; same operation order as the serial code.\ninline double laplacian(const Row& r, size_t x, size_t xp, size_t xn, const Params& P) {\n    const double cv = r.c[x];\n    const double cxx = (r.c[xp] + r.c[xn] - 2.0 * cv) / (P.dx * P.dx);\n    const double cyy = (r.up[x] + r.dn[x] - 2.0 * cv) / (P.dy * P.dy);\n    const double czz = (r.zp[x] + r.zm[x] - 2.0 * cv) / (P.dz * P.dz);\n    return cxx + cyy + czz;\n}\n\n// Chemical potential on owned plane p (1..nzl) from c (ghosts must be valid).\nvoid computeMuPlane(const double* c, double* mu, const Decomp& d, size_t p, const Params& P) {\n    for (size_t y = 0; y < d.ny; ++y) {\n        const Row r = rowAt(c, d, p, y);\n        double* out = mu + p * d.plane + y * d.nx;\n        forEachX(d.nx, [&](size_t x, size_t xp, size_t xn) {\n            const double cv = r.c[x];\n            out[x] = 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * P.e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * P.e_BB - 2.0 * cv * P.e_AB)\n                     + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n                     - P.gamma * laplacian(r, x, xp, xn, P);\n        });\n    }\n}\n\n// Explicit update on owned plane p from cold and mu (mu ghosts must be valid).\nvoid computeCnewPlane(const double* cold, double* cnew, const p * d.plane + y * d.nx;\n        double* out = cnew + p * d.plane + y * d.nx;\n        forEachX(d.nx, [&](size_t x, size_t xp, size_t xn) {\n            out[x] = cr[x] + P.dt * P.D * laplacian(m, x, interior planes.\n    haloStart(d, coldM, reqC);\n    for (size_t p = 2; p < nzl; ++p) {\n        computeMuPlane(cold, mu, d, p, P);\n    }\n    haloFinish(d, coldM, reqC);\n\n    // Phase 2: boundary planes of mu (need c ghosts), then exchange mu ghosts.\n    if (nzl >= 1) computeMuPlane(cold, mu, d, 1, P);\n    if (nzl >= 2) computeMuPlane(cold, mu, d, nzl, P);\n    haloStart(d, mu, reqM);\n\n owned planes; global linear index defines the pseudo-random pattern.\nvoid initializeConcentration(double* c, const Decomp& d) {\n    const size_t vol = d.nx * d.ny * d.nz;\n    for (size_t p = 1; p <= d.nzl; ++p) {\n        const size_t z = d.z0 + (p - 1);\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < d.ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < d.nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = p * d.plane 1) * 1299709) % vol) / static_cast<double>(vol));\n                c[idx] = -1.0 + 2.0 * pseudo;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Gather the owned portions of the field on rank 0 in global z z0 = 0, nzl = 0;\n        planeRange(d.nz, static_cast<size_t>(size), static_cast<size_t>(r), z0, nzl);\n        counts[r] = static_cast<int>(nzl * d.plane);\n        displs[r] = static_cast<int>(z0 * printf(\"  -x <num>     Grid size in X dimension (default: 64)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -y <num>     Grid size in Y dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -z <num>     Grid size in Z = 20;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments (identical on every rank, so all ranks agree on exit)\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-x\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nx = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-y\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            ny = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-z\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nz = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (ny == 0) ny = nx;\n    if (nz == 0) nz = nx;\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Cahn-Hilliard Phase Separation Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Grid size: %zu x %zu x %zu\\n\", nx, ny, nz);\n        printf(\"Time steps: %d\\n\", iterations);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n\n    // Physical parameters\n    const Params P{\n        1.0,                    // dx\n        1.0,                    // dy\n        1.0,                    // dz\n        0.01,                   // dt\n        -(2.0 / 9.0),           // e_AA\n        -(2.0 / 9.0),           // e_BB\n        (2.0 / 9.0),
